violations.text: No person in charge was present (with a certificate from a food safety managers course) as needed at the time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety (with RIDOH Center for Food Protection) at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

An employee was observed washing their hands at the food prep sink. Food employees shall clean their hands in a designated hand-washing sink and not in a food preparation, mop, or ware-washing sink. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026
The hand-washing sink in the ware-washing area was lacking paper towels. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

Molluscan Shellfish tags did not have all of the required information. The last date of sale were lacking. Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

Raw animal foods (such as tuna) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as brussels sprouts) in the safehouse prep unit. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Slicer was moved to ware-washing to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

The following was observed: 1) Broccoli and rabe was observed held at 44-45 degrees Fahrenheit in the safehouse prep unit overnight. Food was voluntarily disposed of by person in charge. 2) Chicken wings was observed held at 42-46 degrees Fahrenheit in the 4 door cooler overnight. Food was voluntarily disposed of by person in charge. 3) Various items in the walk-in cooler were observed at 42-43 degrees in the walk-in cooler (inside). Ambient temperature of walk-in cooler was observed ranging from 41-49 degrees Fahrenheit. PIC to schedule maintenance service for walk-in cooler. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Soup was placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Food was moved to shallow pan and placed into ice bath. Cooling methods reviewed with person in charge. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

Reduced oxygen packaged tuna was observed thawing with the packages in-tact. ROP tuna observed above 38 degrees Fahrenheit were voluntarily disposed of. Tuna observed at 38 degrees and under were removed from the package to properly thaw. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

The door to the outside, located in the back of the kitchen and the door to the outdoor walk-in cooler is not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 10/05/2026

The following was observed: 1) The non-food contact surfaces of the ice machine has an accumulation of pink and black residue. 2) The hood vents were observed with an accumulation of grease. The equipment must be cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the possible contamination of the ice. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026

The shelving and floors in the basement were observed with an accumulation of old rodent droppings. The physical facilities must be cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the possible contamination of food. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2026
The flip top prep unit for "The Safehouse" was observed with a broken door and lid. Per PIC, a maintenance service was placed and is pending repairs. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 10/21/2025
The hand-washing sink (near the cookline) in the kitchen was lacking paper towels. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

The following hand sinks were observed improperly used: 1) The hand sink in the ware washing area was observed with dishes and utensils in it 2) The hand sink at "The Trap" bar was observed with ice and beer 3) The hand sink at "The Safehouse" bar was observed with gloves and other items Hand sinks must be used for hand washing only. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Molluscan Shellfish tags did not have all of the required information: 1) The last date of sale was lacking. 2) Tags were not kept in chronological order. Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Raw animal foods were not stored properly to prevent cross-contamination. Raw beef was observed over raw shrimp. Except when combined as ingredients, different types of raw animal foods must be separated from each other during storage by using separate equipment or arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Slicers were broken down and moved to ware washing area to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Marinara sauce made on site was observed held at 120 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Sauce was reheated to above 165 degrees Fahrenheit. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Various items in the salad prep unit was observed held at 50 degrees Fahrenheit. The ambient temperature of the prep unit was observed at 55 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Per PIC, items were placed in the unit 2 hours prior to inspection. Foods moved to the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Sink and surface solution was observed in excess of 1875 parts per million (ppm). A sink and surface sanitizer solution applied to food contact surfaces must be between 704-1875 ppm. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Meat sauce was observed cooling in the refrigerator in a pan greater than four inches deep. Food moved to shallow pans to properly cool. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

Reduced oxygen packaged tuna was observed thawing with the package in-tact in the walk-in refrigeration. Tuna was observed at 34 degrees Fahrenheit at the time of inspection. Reduced oxygen packaged seafood must be removed from the packaging upon thawing. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025

The following was observed in poor repair: 1) The flip top prep unit for "The Safehouse" was observed with a broken door and lid 2) The unit for both "The Safehouse" and "The Trap" was observed maintaining an ambient temperature of 55 degrees Fahrenheit New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025
The facility is lacking test strips to measure the concentration of the sink and surface sanitizing solution for the 3-bay sink. New Violation. Correct By: 09/23/2025
